_note: THE WATCHED MAN — the twelve-frame storyboard. ONE registry: the pack, the doc and the test are generated from it, never hand-copied.
_note_source: The artist's own 12-frame storyboard for a music video ('THE WATCHED MAN'), pasted 2026-11-06, plus the style reference recovered from the account's own feed.
title: The Watched Man
subtitle: 12 cinematic frames · A man under observation · Belgrade · Analog noir
concept: A man moves through an ordinary day while never quite escaping notice. An institutional corridor at dawn, an observation room, a stairwell where his reflection lags, a crossing where the city smears past him, a café he does not really occupy, an apartment where the instrument stays on the chair, and a rooftop where the sky turns and he is gone. Nothing supernatural happens. The strangeness is in the framing: he is watched, and the watching is in the frame — high angles, empty foregrounds, one light source, and long holds.
figure: One consistent male figure throughout all twelve frames. He does not need to dominate the composition — sometimes he is a silhouette, a reflection, or a small figure in a large institutional space. The moodboard is the house one; the frames are about where the camera is relative to him.
visualDna: 1970s European arthouse cinema, faded Kodak 500T, tobacco browns, dirty teal, nicotine yellow, winter gray, soft halation, analog grain, practical light, natural imperfections, unposed documentary realism, 35mm anamorphic
_note_visualDna: The same house DNA as the NEMA ME U MENI template and the SRCE KUCA set — one film language across the artist's work. The DNA is PALETTE and TEXTURE, and it goes in the prose (the style box), because the artist dictated the style reference separately and the house moodboard codes would be a grade nobody asked for.
dnaProse: 1970s European arthouse, faded Kodak 500T, tobacco browns and dirty teal, nicotine yellow and winter gray, soft halation, analog grain, practical light, unposed documentary realism, 35mm anamorphic
_note_styleReference: MEASURED 2026-11-06, not guessed. The artist pointed at job c6403638 and asked for its look to be set as the style prompt. The probes found: (1) NO server route for a style reference — thirteen candidate paths 404'd while the control route answered 400, so the probe itself worked; (2) every --sref this account uses is an s.mj.run link; (3) job c6403638's own full_command already carries '--sref https://s.mj.run/cATLXOMsR-o --profile ub2pnlv --v 8.2'; (4) the studio's per-image action bar renders that same reference as a thumbnail whose alt IS the URL. So the look the artist pointed at IS this style reference, already minted, and it is a URL.
_note_styleReferenceFlag: MEASURED: the account's style references travel as --sref <url>. The numeric ids (1454119249, 178272779, …) that /api/explore-styles-likes returns are the studio's OWN generated styles — they appear in --sref too, so --sref accepts both a URL and an id. This set uses the URL, because the artist's own job uses the URL and the URL is what the studio's thumbnail points at.
identity: no denim jacket and no leather jacket and no necklace, shaved very short haircut
_note_identity: The house identity clause (docs/VIDEO-FRAMING.md §Step 4). Written once and repeated verbatim, so the set reads as one film rather than twelve pictures.
_note_suffix: The house negation, so signage and lettering stay out of a frame the layout will put type into.
_note_flags: MEASURED against the account's own vocabulary, not assumed. The feed (200 jobs) shows --v 8.2 on 164 jobs and --raw on 85; --ar 16:9 on 101. The '--profile ub2pnlv' on the source job rides on only SIX of 200 jobs, so it is a deliberate grade on that one job rather than the account's default — and the repo's own docs record that the account's personalization is applied to every generation by default. Pinning a default into the registry pins an accident, so it is left out. The repo's config default is '--ar 16:9 --style raw --s 21'; a prompt carrying --raw owns the style slot, so buildFullPrompt drops the config's --style and its coupled --s (verified in the composed command).
_note_renderPlain: MEASURED, docs/VIDEO-FRAMING.md §4: with an --edit attachment every distance clause is disobeyed; without one the camera clause lands. This set is about WHERE THE CAMERA IS — the observation room, the stairwell, the rooftop — so it renders plain and carries the STYLE reference only. A style reference conditions the LOOK; it does not dictate the framing the way an image attachment does.

frames.title: EXT. CORRIDOR, DAWN
frames.beat: The man stands tiny at the far end of a long institutional hallway, back to camera, coat collar up, fluorescent tubes flickering above him.
frames.prose: A long institutional hallway at dawn, fluorescent tubes flickering in their housings, the far end of the corridor lost in a pale grey wash, a man standing very small at the far end with his back to the room and his coat collar turned up
frames.camera: the man small at the far end of the hallway, the empty floor filling the space between, the camera static and square down the corridor
frames.light: one flickering fluorescent tube nearest the camera, the rest of the corridor dimmer

frames.title: INT. OBSERVATION ROOM
frames.beat: A silent wall clock. Below it, the man's motionless hand on a metal table. Nothing moves except the second hand.
frames.prose: A silent wall clock on a bare wall, below it a metal table, a man's motionless hand resting flat on the metal, nothing in the room moving
frames.camera: the clock and the hand on the metal table filling the picture, the rest of the wall plain and empty behind them, the camera at the height of the tabletop
frames.light: one hard overhead source, the wall behind in shadow

frames.title: INT. CORRIDOR — CCTV
frames.beat: The man walks slowly beneath the camera, ghosting at a low frame rate.
frames.prose: A man walking slowly down a bare institutional corridor, his movement smeared into a stepped ghost, the corridor's straight lines running away below him, a ceiling fixture directly above him
frames.camera: seen from the landing above, the man small under the ceiling fixture, the floor plan visible, the corridor's doorways as rectangles below
frames.light: one fluorescent panel overhead, the rest of the corridor dim

frames.title: INT. STAIRWELL — REFLECTION
frames.beat: The man's reflection in a dirty window, misaligned — the reflection lags behind him. He does not turn.
frames.prose: A man's reflection in a grimy stairwell window, the reflection set slightly askew to the man himself, his coat collar up, the stairwell's dirty glass holding both figures at once
frames.camera: the reflection filling the glass and the man small behind it, the stairwell's rail crossing the picture, the camera square on to the window
frames.light: one bare bulb on the landing behind him, the window mostly dark

frames.title: EXT. GREY INTERSECTION
frames.beat: The man motionless at a red crossing, pedestrians smearing past in motion blur. Wet asphalt holds his reflection.
frames.prose: A man standing motionless at a crossing in a grey city street, the people around him smeared into horizontal streaks of motion, wet black asphalt holding his reflection under his feet
frames.camera: the man still in the middle of the picture and the wet asphalt filling the lower half, the streaked pedestrians passing behind him, the camera at street level
frames.light: one overhead street lamp throwing a hard pool onto the crossing

frames.title: INT. DESERTED CAFÉ
frames.beat: Unopened cigarettes on a table, an ashtray, a wall clock. Through the window, the city blurs. The man's silhouette sits just out of frame.
frames.prose: An unopened packet of cigarettes and a heavy glass ashtray on a small café table, a wall clock on the wall behind, the street outside the window reduced to a blur, the edge of a seated figure at the very edge of the picture
frames.camera: the packet and the ashtray in the foreground and the blurred street through the window beyond, the camera at the height of the table
frames.light: one window's daylight behind, the table's front in shadow

frames.title: INT. DARK APARTMENT
frames.beat: Night. The man sits on the floor under a single tungsten lamp, a flugelhorn on a chair beside him. He does not pick it up.
frames.prose: A man sitting on the floor of a dark room at night beside a single tungsten lamp, a flugelhorn resting on a chair next to him, his hands empty and still, the room falling to black past the lamp's reach
frames.camera: the lamp and his hands and half his face in the light, the flugelhorn on the chair beside him, the camera down at the level of the floor
frames.light: one tungsten lamp on the floor beside him, everything else black

frames.title: INT. DOORWAY — DEEP FOCUS
frames.beat: The man stands in a distant doorway, a black rectangle framing him. The flugelhorn remains on the chair in the foreground, out of focus.
frames.prose: A man standing far away in a doorway framed as a black rectangle in a dark room, a flugelhorn on a chair in the foreground thrown out of focus, the room between them empty
frames.camera: the flugelhorn on the chair filling the foreground and the man small in the far doorway, the camera low beside the chair
frames.light: one weak light behind the man in the doorway, the chair and the horn darker

frames.title: INT. ROOM — BEHIND
frames.beat: Behind the musician now — someone plays the flugelhorn from behind, one lamp, an empty chair facing them. We never see the player's face.
frames.prose: A musician playing a flugelhorn seen from behind, their back and the bell of the instrument filling the picture, an empty chair facing them across a small room, one low lamp burning
frames.camera: the player's back and the flugelhorn's bell in the near edge, the empty chair opposite in the middle distance, the camera behind and slightly to the side
frames.light: one low lamp between the chair and the player

frames.title: EXT. ROOFTOP, PRE-DAWN
frames.beat: The man stands at the roof edge holding the flugelhorn, a vast grey sky above. He does not play. The city is silent.
frames.prose: A man standing at the edge of a rooftop holding a flugelhorn in both hands, a vast grey winter sky above the roofline, the city below him dark and without movement
frames.camera: the man small near the edge of the roof and the rooftops and sky filling the rest of the picture, the camera at the height of the roof
frames.light: the flat light of a sky just before dawn, no lamp, no sun

frames.title: EXT. ROOFTOP, DAWN
frames.beat: His face, first clear look — tired, unreadable. Behind him, the sky turns from nicotine yellow to winter grey.
frames.prose: A close view of a man's face on a rooftop at dawn, tired and unreadable, the winter sky behind him changing from nicotine yellow at the horizon to flat grey above, his coat collar up
frames.camera: his face and the sky behind him filling the picture, the roofline low in the frame, the camera square on at his eye level
frames.light: the sky itself the only light, yellow at the horizon and grey above

frames.title: EXT. ROOFTOP, DAWN — FINAL
frames.beat: The man is gone. The flugelhorn rests on the concrete. The camera holds too long.
frames.prose: A flugelhorn lying on the flat concrete of a rooftop at dawn, nobody with it, the winter sky over the roofline, the instrument alone where it was set down
frames.camera: the instrument on the concrete in the foreground and the empty roof and sky filling the rest of the picture, the camera low at the level of the roof
frames.light: the flat light of a winter dawn, the same grey-yellow sky
